title: A Tap, a Hole, a Level

scenes.tts: How can one cell hold a lysosome at P H four point seven and a mitochondrion near eight, in one cytosol? Why does each settle at its own number?
scenes.narration: How can one cell hold a lysosome at pH 4.7 and a mitochondrion near 8, in one cytosol? Why does each settle at its own number?
scenes.caption: How can one cell hold a lysosome at pH 4.7 and a mitochondrion near 8, in one cytosol? Why does each settle at its own number?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film. Colours by concept, held for the whole film and matching the lesson: protons RED-ORANGE dots, calcium TEAL dots, pumps (taps) GOLD, leak (hole and its outflow arrow) GREY, cytosol line WHITE DASHED. Right 60%: a large cell cutaway (soft grey outline that slowly breathes) filling about 75% of frame height, holding five labelled cartoon blocks, no structures: a round lysosome, a stacked Golgi, a folded ER band, a big round nucleus with small gaps in its outline (pores), and one bean-shaped mitochondrion. Faint red-orange dots drift slowly in the cytosol. Left 30%: a vertical number line labelled 'pH', running 4 at the bottom to 8.5 at the top, with a WHITE DASHED horizontal line at 7.2 labelled 'cytosol 7.2'. Show first: on 'a lysosome', the lysosome pulses and a red-orange marker drops onto the ladder at 4.7 with the label 'lysosome'; on 'a mitochondrion', a marker rises to 8 labelled 'matrix'. Dense red-orange dots fill the lysosome, sparse ones the matrix. On 'Why does each settle', the question appears across the top in white: 'Why does each settle at its own number?'

Title 'A Tap, a Hole, a Level' fades in over the top for 2 s, replacing the question text. The world keeps its slow motion: cytosol dots drift, the cell outline breathes, the two ladder markers bob very slightly.

scenes.tts: This is the cell's P H ladder, with typical values from different cells. Each marker is one compartment. The white line is the cytosol. Acid compartments sit below. The matrix, the mitochondrion's inside, sits above.
scenes.narration: This is the cell's pH ladder, with typical values from different cells. Each marker is one compartment. The white line is the cytosol. Acid compartments sit below. The matrix, the mitochondrion's inside, sits above.
scenes.caption: This is the cell's pH ladder, with typical values from different cells. Each marker is one compartment. The white line is the cytosol. Acid compartments sit below. The matrix, the mitochondrion's inside, sits above.
scenes.visual: On 'white line', the dashed cytosol line brightens and a soft white glow sweeps along it; the cytosol region of the cell tints the same faint white for a beat. On 'Acid compartments', three more markers slide from their blocks onto the ladder in turn, each with a thin leader line from block to marker: Golgi 6.6, late endosome 5.5 (a small round block appears near the Golgi), lysosome stays at 4.7. The ladder band below the line tints faint red-orange, labelled 'acid'. On 'the matrix sits above', the band above the line tints faint blue-grey, labelled 'alkaline', and the matrix marker at 8 pulses. On 'Each marker', every marker pulses once in turn with its leader line to its block. A small tag sits under the ladder for the rest of the film: 'typical values, different systems'. The lysosome marker carries a small note: 'midpoint of 4.5 to 5.0'.

scenes.tts: Start with the wall. A membrane lets ions through slowly, but not never. Protons trickle back toward the cytosol.
scenes.narration: Start with the wall. A membrane lets ions through slowly, but not never. Protons trickle back toward the cytosol.
scenes.caption: Start with the wall. A membrane lets ions through slowly, but not never. Protons trickle back toward the cytosol.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes in on the lysosome; the other blocks dim but stay visible at the edges. Its membrane is drawn as a thick grey ring. On 'slowly, but not never', single red-orange dots creep one at a time from inside, through the ring, out into the cytosol: slow, sparse, continuous. A small grey label on the ring: 'leaky wall'.

scenes.tts: Picture the lysosome as a container with a tap and a hole. The tap is a proton pump, the V A T Pase, spending A T P to push protons in.
scenes.narration: Picture the lysosome as a container with a tap and a hole. The tap is a proton pump, the V-ATPase, spending ATP to push protons in.
scenes.caption: Picture the lysosome as a container with a tap and a hole. The tap is a proton pump, the V-ATPase, spending ATP to push protons in.
scenes.visual: The ring morphs into a tall upright container (same place, same grey outline), about 60% of frame height, with a GOLD tap at the top left labelled 'V-ATPase (tap)' and a small GREY hole near the bottom right labelled 'leak (hole)'. The ladder stays at left, with the lysosome marker now reset to the cytosol line at 7.2. On 'the V A T Pase' (caption 'V-ATPase'), the tap opens and a steady stream of red-orange dots falls in from the cytosol side, drawn as a GOLD arrow of fixed length labelled 'pump in'.

No words: show before telling. The red-orange level inside the container rises steadily. A GREY outflow arrow at the hole starts short and lengthens as the level rises; dots spill out of the hole faster. The ladder marker sinks from 7.2 toward 5.5 in step with the level. Corner tag: 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: As protons pile up, more leak back out through the hole. At some level, out matches in, and the level stops rising. This picture needs no sensor to set that level.
scenes.narration: As protons pile up, more leak back out through the hole. At some level, out matches in, and the level stops rising. This picture needs no sensor to set that level.
scenes.caption: As protons pile up, more leak back out through the hole. At some level, out matches in, and the level stops rising. This picture needs no sensor to set that level.
scenes.visual: Continue the same motion, slowing: the grey outflow arrow grows until it is exactly the length of the gold inflow arrow; on 'out matches in', a small '=' sign appears between the two arrows and both glow. The level stops rising and holds with a gentle ripple on its surface; the ladder marker settles back at its rung. No dial icon. Level curve inset (small, lower right): a smooth rise-then-flatten curve of level against time, endpoint unlabelled, tagged 'qualitative toy model'.

scenes.tts: That is the idea, for this acid lumen. The level sits where pumping in meets leaking out. Other things equal, a stronger pump makes it more acid. A leakier wall makes it less acid.
scenes.narration: That is the idea, for this acid lumen. The level sits where pumping in meets leaking out. Other things equal, a stronger pump makes it more acid. A leakier wall makes it less acid.
scenes.caption: That is the idea, for this acid lumen. The level sits where pumping in meets leaking out. Other things equal, a stronger pump makes it more acid. A leakier wall makes it less acid.
scenes.visual: The rule appears across the top in white, one phrase at a time: 'level = where pumping in meets leaking out'. On 'a stronger pump', the gold tap widens, the inflow arrow lengthens, the level rises to a new resting height and the ladder marker sinks a little (label 'more acid'). On 'A leakier wall', the tap returns to normal and the grey hole widens instead: the outflow arrow jumps, the level falls, the marker climbs toward the line (label 'less acid'). Then both return to the baseline. Corner tag: 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Now a drug, bafilomycin, clamps the V A T Pase tap shut. Watch the ladder. Which way will the lysosome's marker move, up or down?
scenes.narration: Now a drug, bafilomycin, clamps the V-ATPase tap shut. Watch the ladder. Which way will the lysosome's marker move, up or down?
scenes.caption: Now a drug, bafilomycin, clamps the V-ATPase tap shut. Watch the ladder. Which way will the lysosome's marker move, up or down?
scenes.visual: A small block labelled 'bafilomycin' slides in and clamps onto the gold tap; the tap turns dull and the inflow arrow vanishes. Freeze nothing else: the surface still ripples. On 'Which way', the lysosome marker on the ladder pulses, with a white question mark beside it and two faint arrows, one up and one down. Question card at top: 'Tap off: which way does the marker go?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. The container holds still except for the slow ripple and a slow pulse on the ladder marker. Nothing drains yet.

scenes.tts: Up, toward the line: less acid. With the tap off, the hole keeps draining. In HeLa cells, bafilomycin made the Golgi less acid. So that acid is actively kept.
scenes.narration: Up, toward the line: less acid. With the tap off, the hole keeps draining. In HeLa cells, bafilomycin made the Golgi less acid. So that acid is actively kept.
scenes.caption: Up, toward the line: less acid. With the tap off, the hole keeps draining. In HeLa cells, bafilomycin made the Golgi less acid. So that acid is actively kept.
scenes.visual: On 'Up', the level starts falling as grey outflow continues and the outflow arrow shortens as the level drops; the ladder marker climbs from its rung toward the white cytosol line, with the label 'less acid'. It does not snap onto the line. On 'In HeLa cells', a small Golgi container slides in beside the lysosome with its own clamped tap; its marker climbs from 6.6 toward the line. Label under it: 'HeLa cells: Golgi less acid'. On 'actively kept', both taps unclamp and their levels refill to their rungs (reset for the next scene).

scenes.tts: The Golgi uses the same pump family, yet it settles higher, near six point six. Does the lysosome have more pumps, a tighter wall, or something else? That is still being worked out.
scenes.narration: The Golgi uses the same pump family, yet it settles higher, near six point six. Does the lysosome have more pumps, a tighter wall, or something else? That is still being worked out.
scenes.caption: The Golgi uses the same pump family, yet it settles higher, near six point six. Does the lysosome have more pumps, a tighter wall, or something else? That is still being worked out.
scenes.visual: Golgi and lysosome containers side by side, same size, with generic, non-quantitative gold pump and grey efflux symbols (tag: 'icons are not quantitative; the differing mechanisms are unresolved'). Both run, and each level settles: Golgi at 6.6, lysosome at its rung, with ladder markers moving in step. On 'more pumps', a second ghost tap flickers on the lysosome; on 'a tighter wall', its hole flickers smaller; on 'something else', a white question mark appears between the containers. Neither change is kept: both containers return to the generic icons. Label: 'which differs? still studied'.

scenes.tts: The nucleus is different. Its envelope is full of pores, and small ions, protons included, pass through them quickly. So its P H stays close to the cytosol's.
scenes.narration: The nucleus is different. Its envelope is full of pores, and small ions, protons included, pass through them quickly. So its pH stays close to the cytosol's.
scenes.caption: The nucleus is different. Its envelope is full of pores, and small ions, protons included, pass through them quickly. So its pH stays close to the cytosol's.
scenes.visual: The camera pulls back to the cell; the nucleus becomes a container whose wall is drawn with many gaps (pores). No tap. Small red-orange dots pass freely through the gaps in both directions, inside and outside at the same density. The nucleus marker sits just beside the white dashed line, labelled 'nucleus: near 7.2'.

scenes.tts: The E R is also a nonequilibrium store. A calcium pump called SERCA fills it to thousands of times the cytosol's level, while leaks and release channels move calcium out.
scenes.narration: The ER is also a nonequilibrium store. A calcium pump called SERCA fills it to thousands of times the cytosol's level, while leaks and release channels move calcium out.
scenes.caption: The ER is also a nonequilibrium store. A calcium pump called SERCA fills it to thousands of times the cytosol's level, while leaks and release channels move calcium out.
scenes.visual: Same container picture, now for the ER, drawn in TEAL: a container with a gold tap labelled 'SERCA (tap)' and a grey hole. Teal dots pour in and the teal level rises high; a teal gauge beside it (replacing the pH ladder for this scene, same position, log scale labelled 'free calcium') shows the ER marker far above a 'cytosol' mark, with the label 'thousands of times higher'. Corner tag on the container: 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Thapsigargin, a plant compound, blocks SERCA. Calcium keeps leaking out, and nothing pumps it back. The store runs down, and cytosol calcium rises for a while.
scenes.narration: Thapsigargin, a plant compound, blocks SERCA. Calcium keeps leaking out, and nothing pumps it back. The store runs down, and cytosol calcium rises for a while.
scenes.caption: Thapsigargin, a plant compound, blocks SERCA. Calcium keeps leaking out, and nothing pumps it back. The store runs down, and cytosol calcium rises for a while.
scenes.visual: A block labelled 'thapsigargin' clamps onto the SERCA tap; inflow stops. Teal dots keep streaming out of the grey hole, the ER level falls, and the ER marker on the teal gauge drops toward the cytosol mark. As they leave, the cytosol around the ER briefly fills with extra teal dots (cytosol marker on the gauge rises), then they thin out again. Tag: 'schematic'. Then the teal gauge slides away and the pH ladder returns.

scenes.tts: The mitochondrion's pumps face the other way. They are the respiratory chain, driven by electron transport. While it runs, they push protons out of the matrix, so the matrix sits above the line.
scenes.narration: The mitochondrion's pumps face the other way. They are the respiratory chain, driven by electron transport. While it runs, they push protons out of the matrix, so the matrix sits above the line.
scenes.caption: The mitochondrion's pumps face the other way. They are the respiratory chain, driven by electron transport. While it runs, they push protons out of the matrix, so the matrix sits above the line.
scenes.visual: Before the words, the camera moves to the mitochondrion, drawn as a container whose inside is the matrix. Its gold taps, labelled 'respiratory chain (taps)', with a small label 'while respiring', are mounted pointing OUTWARD: red-orange dots are pushed from the matrix out across the inner membrane, and a few leak back in through a grey hole. The matrix dot density thins, and its ladder marker climbs above the white line and settles at 8. On 'the other way', the arrow direction flips are highlighted: lysosome taps point in, mitochondrion taps point out, shown side by side in miniature.

scenes.tts: Why the other way? The matrix was once a bacterium's cytoplasm, and during respiration its electron-transport chain pumped protons outward.
scenes.narration: Why the other way? The matrix was once a bacterium's cytoplasm, and during respiration its electron-transport chain pumped protons outward.
scenes.caption: Why the other way? The matrix was once a bacterium's cytoplasm, and during respiration its electron-transport chain pumped protons outward.
scenes.visual: The mitochondrion's outer outline fades, and the inner membrane morphs into a free rod-shaped bacterium drifting on its own (label 'free-living bacterium, long ago'); its inside is labelled 'cytoplasm', and the same gold taps push red-orange dots out of it. Then it is engulfed by a host-cell outline and morphs back into the mitochondrion in the same place, label 'cytoplasm' becoming 'matrix'. Tag: 'cartoon'.

scenes.tts: Chloroplasts did the same. Their stroma, the fluid inside, was once a cyanobacterium's cytoplasm, and in light it turns alkaline. Every proton pump here pushes out of a cytoplasm.
scenes.narration: Chloroplasts did the same. Their stroma, the fluid inside, was once a cyanobacterium's cytoplasm, and in light it turns alkaline. Every proton pump here pushes out of a cytoplasm.
scenes.caption: Chloroplasts did the same. Their stroma, the fluid inside, was once a cyanobacterium's cytoplasm, and in light it turns alkaline. Every proton pump here pushes out of a cytoplasm.
scenes.visual: A green-outlined chloroplast block slides in below the mitochondrion; on 'in light', a lamp icon brightens and gold taps push red-orange dots out of the stroma into small stacked inner sacs; a stroma marker rises on the ladder to the 7.8 to 8.0 band, labelled 'stroma, in light'. On 'Every proton pump', three miniatures line up: lysosome (tap points from cytosol into lumen), mitochondrion and chloroplast (taps point out of matrix and stroma); each source side flashes with the label 'a cytoplasm'.

scenes.tts: The acid lumens, the matrix and the stroma need ongoing energy-dependent transport. Acid lumens need their V A T Pase. The matrix and stroma need respiration or light. Stop that input, and those gradients run down.
scenes.narration: The acid lumens, the matrix and the stroma need ongoing energy-dependent transport. Acid lumens need their V-ATPase. The matrix and stroma need respiration or light. Stop that input, and those gradients run down.
scenes.caption: The acid lumens, the matrix and the stroma need ongoing energy-dependent transport. Acid lumens need their V-ATPase. The matrix and stroma need respiration or light. Stop that input, and those gradients run down.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: cell cutaway right, ladder left with all markers (lysosome 4.7, late endosome 5.5, Golgi 6.6, cytosol line 7.2 with nucleus just beside it, stroma about 7.9, matrix 8), tag 'typical values, different systems'. Gold taps appear only where the lesson names a pump: V-ATPase taps on Golgi, late endosome and lysosome pointing in; respiratory-chain taps on the mitochondrion and light-driven taps on the chloroplast pointing out. Nucleus and ER have no taps. Levels ripple. On 'Stop paying', those taps dim and their markers drift toward the white dashed line (acid ones up, matrix and stroma down), labelled 'run down'; none snaps exactly onto the line. Nucleus and ER markers stay where they are. The hook's question returns faintly at the top, then fades.

scenes.line: The gradients shown here need ongoing energy-dependent transport.
scenes.visual: End card in large white text over the dimmed world: 'The gradients shown here need ongoing energy-dependent transport.' Behind it the taps slowly turn back on and the markers return to their rungs.
